metadata.title: NVDA Stock: Where Compounding Could Take The Price

content.text:
This is no longer just a chip company; it is becoming the central bank for the AI revolution. NVIDIA is helping establish financing platforms to raise over $500 billion of third-party capital for its customers. It has also directly invested nearly $50 billion in the Frontier AI labs, effectively underwriting its own demand.
This new role as financier directly fuels the revenue engine. The non-hyperscaler ACIE segment now represents about half of the business and is growing 100% a year. That compounding is what drives the upside case from here.
That's the story for NVIDIA (NVDA). The question is whether it's strong enough to deliver real upside from here, or whether today's price has already absorbed most of the optimism. Mostly yes. A conservative 3-year scenario points to roughly 57% of upside in NVDA, and the operational story carries it. The earnings line is moving in the right direction, but a softer multiple is set to chew a meaningful chunk of that out before it reaches the stock. Here is the operational picture the math sits on top of:
*LTM: Last Twelve Months
How Compounding Builds The Upside
Revenue compounds at 30% annually, taking the top line from $303.0B to $665.6B over three years. That is a further step down from the LTM 83% pace, in line with the deceleration the business is already showing.
Margins ease from 64% to 61% as today's LTM reverts partway toward the 3-year average of 54%. Together that takes earnings from $192.9B to roughly $404.8B, a 110% jump.
Here is where the stock and the earnings line diverge. NVDA's P/E already sits at 27.3x, below its 3-year average of 41.6x. The scenario trims it further to 20.5x, because a slower forward growth rate no longer supports even today's multiple. That single move chews roughly 25% out of what the earnings growth would otherwise have delivered. Apply the lower multiple to the higher earnings and the stock lands near $342.46, a market cap of $8.3T against $5.3T today. That is roughly 57% above where the stock trades now. The earnings line is doing the work; the multiple is taking a meaningful cut of it before it reaches the share price.
Has revenue compounding been the lever driving NVDA's recent move? See the lever breakdown.
What Could Accelerate The Top Line
Beyond current GPU dominance, a second major hardware business is rapidly scaling. Management's preliminary expectation is for CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal '28. This expansion could make NVIDIA one of the world's leading server CPU suppliers, adding a significant new layer to the revenue story.
